title: service-api/1 — the /translate contract
description: The one contract between a translation service and what calls it. Servers: nmt-forge serve, mt-eval serve, or anyone's (a method of kind `service`). Client: the champollion CLI's `api` method (sync, translate, serve). POST /translate takes a translate_request and answers 200 with a translate_response (207 when some keys failed, listed under `errors`), or an error_response (400 a request it cannot take, 401 a missing or wrong token, 404 an unknown route, 413 too large, 500 the method failed — never a partial answer). GET /health answers a health document. A field a server does not use is ignored, never refused. What a service writes can carry what it learned from: a server whose health says output_local_only true puts output_local_only true in the meta of every translate_response, and a client writes such output only where the data's holders agreed. Held to shared/test-fixtures/framework/service-api-vectors.json.

keys.description: key → the source string to translate. Keys are the caller's (app message ids); values that are not non-empty strings come back under `errors`.

source_locale.description: Optional: the server refuses a language it does not translate from.

target_locale.description: Optional: the server refuses a language it does not translate into.

method.description: The method the caller expects; a server serving one method may ignore it.

text_format.description: Set for document text (Markdown); unset for app strings. A server that does not know it treats the text as plain.

instructions.description: key → a note for that key (plural form, a gate's retry reason). Sent only to a server declared to follow them (accepts_instructions).

translations.description: key → the translation, for every key that did not fail.

errors.description: key → why that key was not translated (status 207).

meta.description: What produced the answer. Open: a server adds its own fields (cost_usd, note, decode_hook).

pair.description: source→target, as the server names them.

output_gates.description: What the server checks in what it returns, said in words — 'none — …' when it checks nothing.

output_local_only.description: true: what it writes may repeat sentences marked local-only, so it stays on this machine unless the data's holders agree. false: nothing it learned from is marked so. null: not known (said as such, never guessed).

holders_agreed_by.description: Who among the data's holders agreed that local-only output may be served on an address other machines reach; null when it is not (a local-only server is refused that address without it).
